author: Pallas, 1776
status: 나그네새, 해마다 수천 마리 · 겨울에도 드물게 기록
habitat: 해안 갯벌, 염전, 강 하구, 해안 사구

months.note: 봄에는 4월 초~5월 말, 가을에는 7월 말~10월 중순에 보인다.

summary: 봄과 가을에 비교적 흔하게 지나가는 나그네새이다. 해안의 갯벌, 염전, 강 하구, 해안 사구 등에서 작은 무리를 지어 다른 물떼새류와 섞여 지내며 주로 갯지렁이를 먹는다. 파미르, 티베트, 캄차카, 추코트반도에서 번식하고 아프리카 동부, 인도, 동남아시아, 뉴질랜드, 호주에서 겨울을 난다.

points.en: breeding: black forehead band, eye-stripe and ear-coverts

young: 성조 겨울깃과 비슷하지만 몸 윗면에 비늘 무늬가 있고 얼굴과 가슴에 황갈색 기운이 돈다.

similar.how: 매우 비슷하지만 왕눈물떼새는 부리가 더 짧다.
왕눈물떼새 겨울깃은 흰물떼새 암컷과 비슷하나 목 뒤에 흰색이 없다.

art.subject: Siberian Sand Plover (Charadrius mongolus), adult male in breeding plumage, as seen on Korean tidal flats in April and May: black mask from the bill base through the eye to the ear-coverts, joined to a black bar across the forecrown above a white forehead patch; crown and upperparts plain grey-brown; throat white, bordered below by a thin black line; broad rufous-orange band across the breast, continuing up the sides of the neck onto the hindneck; belly and undertail white. Bill short, stout and entirely black. Eye dark. Legs dark grey-green.
art.pose: foraging on a mudflat, pulling a ragworm from the mud
art.scene: Korean tidal mudflat in spring with a small mixed flock of plovers; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male breeding (April–May), side view standing: black mask and forecrown bar, white forehead and throat, broad rufous-orange breast band reaching the hindneck, short all-black bill, dark grey-green legs

adult non-breeding (August–October), side view standing: grey-brown upperparts, white forehead and supercilium, dark brown lores and ear-coverts, grey-brown patches at the breast sides, no white hind collar, short black bill
juvenile (August–September), side view standing: scaly grey-brown upperparts with buff fringes, buff wash on the face and breast sides, no white hind collar
art.build: Small-medium plover, 19.5cm, clearly larger than Little Ringed Plover and smaller than Grey Plover. Rounded head with a steep forehead, short neck, compact body. Bill black, short and blunt, shorter than the head and noticeably shorter than in Greater Sand Plover. Legs medium length, dark grey to greenish-grey. At rest the wingtips reach about the tail tip. In flight a narrow white wing bar and white sides to the dark-centred rump and tail. Forages on open mud by run-stop-peck, often pulling out worms.
avoid: Do not paint a longer, heavier bill or pale yellowish legs — that is Greater Sand Plover (Charadrius leschenaultii).
Do not paint a white hind collar; Kentish Plover has one, this species does not.
Do not paint a black breast band; the breeding band is rufous-orange.
Do not paint a yellow eye-ring or orange legs.
